content: Tepezcohuite, pronounced as Te-pez-Co-wheete, is derived from the bark of the Mimosa tenuiflora tree, native to Mexico. In Mexico, it is often referred to as the Skin Tree due to its notable properties, which include acting as an antimicrobial agent, an analgesic, and a cellular regenerator. Extracts of Tepezcohuite contain flavonoids, which reduce capillary permeability, enhance capillary resistance, and provide protection against skin aging. Additionally, it contains tannins, which exhibit astringent properties that help smooth the skin. The bark is also rich in micronutrients such as zinc, copper, manganese, iron, and magnesium, all of which play critical roles in cellular repair and protection. Extensive research conducted in laboratories in Mexico, Canada, and the United Kingdom has demonstrated that Tepezcohuite functions as a cellular regenerator, an antibacterial agent that is 300% more effective than streptomycin, and a potent fungicide. Uses for Tepezcohuite Tepezcohuite is considered to have antiseptic, analgesic, and cellular regeneration-promoting properties. However, not all of its uses have been experimentally verified for efficacy or safety. It is essential to consult a medical professional before using it in any form. Burns Tepezcohuite may provide protection for firstand second-degree burns by preventing fluid loss. It may also inhibit the formation of keloidal scars and support the regeneration of hair follicles. Traumatology In cases of traumatic injuries, Tepezcohuite is believed to protect exposed bone and aid in the regeneration of soft tissue. It also exhibits antiseptic properties, though studies suggest it is no more effective than current antiseptics. Additionally, there is evidence that it may have toxic effects on the liver. Dermatology Tepezcohuite may help prevent wrinkles and acne. It has also been suggested as a treatment for conditions such as psoriasis, herpes simplex virus types I and II, and chickenpox scars. Cosmetology Beyond its dermatological benefits, Tepezcohuite may protect and stimulate the production of collagen and elastin. It also contains protective flavonoids and hyaluronic acid, which contribute to skin health and regeneration.
